newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan key 3-mth CD rate rises to 0.70 pct.
newsitem.headline: Japan key 3-mth CD rate rises to 0.70 pct.

text.p: Japan's key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) rate rose to 0.70 percent in early afternoon on Tuesday, the highest rate since August 7, 1996, traders said.
The rate jumped sharply from the previous 0.64 percent as issuers of the three-month CDs were eager to raise long-term funds to cover the end-September interim fiscal year-end, they said.
The previously issued three-month CDs at 0.64 percent are due to mature before the end of September. No three-month CDs have been issued since Thursday last week.
The issued volume at 0.70 percent so far on Tuesday was around 130 billion yen, traders said.
Given the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) more accommodative money market operation this morning than recently, some investors gave in and lowered their bids from around 0.75 percent, they said.

The BOJ's operation left the market with a fund surplus of some 400 billion yen, the first such accommodative operation since March 31, the last day of the fiscal 1996/97. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
